extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literary criticism and creative writing (lecture audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for recognizing and producing 'heroic' greatness and true poetry: what makes a Hero, Prophet, or Poet powerful, sincere, and enduring in literature and life. Emphasizes sincerity, depth of vision, musicality, seriousness, and symbolic embodiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity (authenticity of voice and vision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sincerity ... is the first and last merit in a book; ... it alone can give rise to merit of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carlyle stresses 'sincerity of vision' and a 'sincere heart' as fundamental: the work/author must show direct, first-hand insight rather than hearsay or polished insincerity. Anti-patterns include the smooth-polished, respectable insincere man ('the insincere man: smooth-polished, respectable ... just as carbonic acid is, which is death and poison').

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct insight / 'eye that flashes direct into the heart of things'
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet/prophet must have an eye for the world: he 'brings home still, to our heart, the thing his own heart has been opened to.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued is immediate, rugged vigor of perception — 'glance as of the real thinker and seer.' Works should display concrete, vivid perceptions that convince by directness rather than abstract generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical thought / musicality
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is 'musical Thought' — if your delineation be authentically musical, musical not in word only, but in heart and substance, then it will be poetical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Musicality means inward harmony, melody, and rhythm in thought and expression. It is not merely metrical ornament but coherence and 'melody' at the level of conception and feeling. Passionate language naturally becomes chant-like — a sign of musical thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of vision / penetration of the 'open secret'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vates (Poet/Prophet) has penetrated into 'the open secret' — the divine mystery or 'the Divine Idea of the World' that lies at the bottom of appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A great writer reveals the underlying unity or spiritual truth of things; this depth is tied to sincerity and cannot be faked. The poet's role is to make that mystery impressively known to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnestness / seriousness (opposed to dilettantism)
rubrics_metrics.description: No Dilettantism in this Mahomet; it is a business of Reprobation and Salvation ... he is in deadly earnest about it! Dilettantism ... is the sorest sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works and authors must show total commitment and moral/creative seriousness. Amateurish speculation, coquetting with truth, or superficial play is condemned as fatal to greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty / freedom from cant
rubrics_metrics.description: Withal I like Mahomet for his total freedom from cant. He is a rough self-helping son of the wilderness; does not pretend to be what he is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid hypocrisy, performative humility, or artificial piety; candor and plain speech that match inward conviction are prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral earnestness / tendency to good
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not praise Mahomet's moral precepts as always of the superfinest sort; yet it can be said that there is always a tendency to good in them; that they are the true dictates of a heart aiming towards what is just and true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work's ethical orientation — a discernible tendency toward what is just and humane — strengthens its stature. Moral complexity is acceptable, but an underlying direction toward genuine good is valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to awaken the Heroic in readers (transformative power)
rubrics_metrics.description: Kindle the inner genial life of him, you have a flame that burns up all lower considerations. Difficulty, abnegation, martyrdom, death are the allurements that act on the heart of man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great writing or belief awakens higher, heroic impulses in ordinary people; it must show avenues for noble action and self-transcendence rather than merely seducing appetite or ease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of concrete, symbolic embodiment (emblems of truth)
rubrics_metrics.description: That gross sensual Paradise ... that horrible flaming Hell ... what is all this but a rude shadow ... of that grand spiritual Fact ... the Infinite Nature of Duty? ... Bodied forth in what way you will, it is the first of all truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic or concrete imagery (even if culturally 'gross') can validly embody profound, universal truths; the form is venerable so long as it conveys a deeper spiritual or moral reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-discipline / resistance to habit (moral formation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a man assert withal that he is king over his habitudes; that he could and would shake them off, on cause shown: this is an excellent law. The Month Ramadhan ... bears in that direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A heroic creator or character demonstrates self-control and deliberate self-limitation; moral training/abnegation is presented as a virtue rather than simple indulgence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of triviality and sceptical dilettantism
rubrics_metrics.description: Sceptical Dilettantism, the curse of these ages ... makes sad work; and our reverence for great men ... comes out in poor plight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works should resist fashionable trivialism and shallowness; seriousness and faith in the reality of greatness are prerequisites for producing or recognizing true poetic/heroic art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal scope / capacity to be 'believed' and lived by
rubrics_metrics.description: Above all things, it has been a religion heartily believed. These Arabs believe their religion, and try to live by it! ... Belief is great, life-giving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural or literary creations that can command genuine belief or guide life over time achieve significance; persuasiveness and practical force (not mere novelty) are metrics of value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence / inward harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: A musical thought ... detected the inmost mystery of it, namely the melody that lies hidden in it; the inward harmony of coherence which is its soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond ornament, a successful work must exhibit inner coherence — parts harmonizing to reveal the whole. This is central to poetic effect and 'musical' thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth and versatility of genius
rubrics_metrics.description: I have no notion of a truly great man that could not be all sorts of men. The grand fundamental character is that of Great Man; that the man be great.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great creators often display potential across multiple spheres (poet, statesman, thinker). A sense of broad capability or comprehensiveness in outlook is a sign of greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passion in language (expressive intensity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe too how all passionate language does of itself become musical ... the speech of a man even in zealous anger becomes a chant, a song.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional intensity and conviction in diction tend to produce musical, moving expression; passion is a tool for achieving poetic effect when allied to depth and sincerity.
